findings.reason: src/Set.js:107 now always calls SetCollection(iters[ii]).forEach, and the diff deletes the typeof === 'string' branch, so Set([1]).union('abc') now adds 'a','b','c' where the baseline added 'abc'. The behaviour change is real. Whether it is a defect depends on story.md, which is not in the packet or the export (the CHANGELOG doesn't mention it either), so the code can't tell us if the change was intended.
findings.claim: Removing the string special case makes Set#union split a string argument into characters instead of adding the whole string.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (typeof iters[ii] === 'string') { set.add(iters[ii]); } else {...}` and keeps only `SetCollection(iters[ii]).forEach(value => set.add(value));`. SetCollection iterates a string by character, so `Set([1]).union('abc')` now yields {1,'a','b','c'} where the baseline yielded {1,'abc'}. No story.md exists in the packet or export, so the intended behaviour can't be checked against a spec.
